title: Lesson 1: Starting Point

intro.title: Starting Point
intro.lead: Answer these once, right after Lesson 1. Don't try to make them sound impressive. Honest answers are the useful ones. You'll come back to these at the end of Module 1 and compare them with your finished Business Foundation Blueprint.

fields.label: 1. What have you been treating as your blogging business?
fields.guide: Name where most of your time and energy has gone so far. Your blog posts, Instagram, Pinterest views, your website design, or something else.
fields.example: My blog posts and Pinterest. I've been measuring progress by pageviews and how my homepage looks.

fields.label: 2. What do you ultimately want someone to pay you for?
fields.guide: You don't need the exact product yet. Describe the result, transformation, or solution you want to provide, and who it's for if you already know.
fields.example: Helping overwhelmed moms keep their homes organized with young kids. Probably a simple system. Not sure of the format yet.

fields.label: 3. If your blog disappeared tomorrow, would you still have a business idea?
fields.guide: Start with yes, no, or partly. Then write what you would still know: who you want to help, the problem you want to solve, and what you could sell. If the answer is no, that's okay. That's exactly what Module 1 is for.
fields.example: Partly. I know who I want to help. I don't know the exact problem they'd pay to fix or what I'd sell.

fields.label: 4. Your Biggest Realization
fields.guide: After Lesson 1, what do you understand differently about building a blogging business? One or two sentences is enough.
fields.example: I've been creating content and hoping it turns into a business. I need to start with the person and the problem.

footer_note: You’ll read these answers again in Lesson 9.
